title: Flag
description: A feature flag is a conditional toggle that lets you control who sees a feature without deploying code.

title: Segment
description: A segment is a reusable group of users defined by attribute rules (e.g., 'beta testers' or 'enterprise customers').

title: Environment
description: An environment is an isolated context for flag states (e.g., Development, Staging, Production).

title: Project
description: A project groups related flags, segments, and environments together — typically one per application or service.

title: Targeting Rule
description: A targeting rule defines who gets which flag value based on user attributes (e.g., 'email contains @test.com → true').

title: Percentage Rollout
description: A percentage rollout gradually exposes a flag to a random percentage of users (0–100%).

title: Release Toggle
description: A release toggle decouples deployment from release — ship code dark and enable it when ready.

title: Experiment Toggle
description: An experiment toggle powers A/B tests by randomly assigning users to variants and measuring outcomes.

title: Ops Toggle
description: An ops toggle controls operational behavior — maintenance mode, feature kill switches, or rate limiting.

title: Permission Toggle
description: A permission toggle gates features based on user tier, plan, or role — like 'admin-only preview'.

title: Active
description: The flag is live and actively evaluating. This is the normal operating state.

title: Rolled Out
description: The flag has been fully rolled out to 100% and is awaiting cleanup.

title: Deprecated
description: The flag is marked for removal. It may still evaluate but should not be used in new code.

title: Archived
description: The flag has been removed from active use and is preserved for audit purposes only.

title: API Key
description: An API key authenticates SDK requests. Server-side keys have full access; client-side keys are environment-scoped.

title: Webhook
description: A webhook sends HTTP callbacks to your server when flag states change — keeping your systems in sync.

title: Audit Log
description: The audit log records every change to flags, segments, and settings — who did what, when, and from where.

title: Toggle Category
description: The type of toggle: Release (ship dark), Experiment (A/B test), Ops (operational), or Permission (access control).

title: Condition
description: A condition matches users based on attributes (e.g., 'country equals US' or 'plan in [pro, enterprise]').

title: Variant
description: A variant is a named value in a multi-armed experiment (e.g., 'control', 'treatment-a', 'treatment-b').

title: SDK
description: The FeatureSignals SDK integrates with your application to evaluate flags at runtime.

title: Evaluation
description: Evaluation is the process of determining which flag value to serve for a given user at runtime.

title: Janitor
description: Janitor is FeatureSignals' automated stale flag detection and cleanup system.

title: Kill Switch
description: A kill switch is an ops toggle that can instantly disable a feature in production during an incident.
